newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rubber firm to expand ahead of listing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rubber firm to expand ahead of listing.

text.p: Indonesia's largest latex and rubber products manufacturer, state-owned PT Perkebunan Nusantara III, said on Wednesday it expected to sharply expand production ahead of its 1998 listing on local bourses.

"Raising the production capacity is absolutely necessary as demand is so strong. Some customers in Europe have even asked us to expedite our expansion programme to meet the rising demand," production director Umar Lubis told Reuters.
He said the expansion was part of efforts to boost financial performance before Nusantara III's planned listing on Surabaya and Jakarta stock exchanges.
Lubis said Nusantara III expected to book revenues totalling around 500 billion rupiah in 1996. He did not give comparative figures.
Lubis and marketing director Meganada, however, declined to say how many shares will be listed.
Both said the firm was making preparations for the listing and were upbeat on it.
Meganada said the expansion would include raising production capacity of its glove and rubber thread factories and setting up a glue factory using low-grade latex.
"We expect to sharply raise our annual production capacity of rubber gloves to 300 million pieces in the fourth quarter of next year from the current 50 million," Lubis said.
He said the firm expected to start building up its glove production facilities next January.
Lubis also said Nusantara III planned to expand its rubber thread production capacity by 3,000 tonnes to 10,500 tonnes per year in 1998.
Rubber thread is widely used in the manufacturing of clothing, automotive parts and medical equipment.
He said Nusantara III was negotiating with a local firm to set up a lubricant oil producing plant using low-grade latex from its plantations.
"The firm is going to be the first in the world producing lubricants using latex," he said without elaborating.
He said the venture was likely to cost some $50 million and construction was expected to begin in 1998.
The supply of latex needed for the expansion in production of rubber products was unlikely to be a problem as the firm had plantations covering some 166,000 hectares in north Sumatra, he said.
Nusantara III is expected to source all its latex needs from its own plantations, but would not rule out buying from other sources within Indonesia, he said.
He said the firm produced 55,000 tonnes of latex in 1995 and expected production to remain stable this year.
